audits.title: The Effect of an Education Session on Medication Documentation Quality in a Model 2 Irish Hospital: a Closed Loop Audit
audits.standard: Adapted MediDocQ patient safety instrument for prescribing and transcribing documentation
audits.setting: Model 2 hospital (University Hospital Limerick affiliation), inpatients

cycle1.result: As-required prescribing completeness 35%; discontinuation completeness 21%; allergy status documented 90%; nature of reaction documented 43%.

cycle2.result: As-required prescribing completeness 33%; discontinuation completeness 31%; allergy status 100%; nature of reaction 31%.

audits.other_findings: No convincing or consistent improvement; polypharmacy 76% and hyperpolypharmacy 46%.
audits.citation: Fernandes L, Eltayeb E, Mustafa M, Gabr A, Mohamed A, Lonappan A, et al.. The Effect of an Education Session on Medication Documentation Quality in a Model 2 Irish Hospital: a Closed Loop Audit. Age and Ageing. 2025;54(Supplement_4). doi:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.150.

audits.title: 314 Audit on Prescription Legibility in an Irish University Teaching Hospital
audits.standard: HSE Standards and Recommended Practices for Healthcare Records Management; Practice Standards and Guidelines for Nurses for Prescriptive Authority

cycle1.result: 48% of drug kardexes legible; 68% on medical vs 19% on surgical wards (p<0.05); upper case used in 13%.

audits.other_findings: Planned targeted prescribing education, kardex layout changes and electronic prescribing.
audits.citation: McCarthy C, Sebaoui S, Saif K, Murphy E, Roy A, Hynes J, et al.. 314 Audit on Prescription Legibility in an Irish University Teaching Hospital. Age and Ageing. 2019;48(Supplement_3):iii17-iii65. doi:10.1093/ageing/afz103.203.

audits.title: P37 Audit on the quality of documentation of paediatric prescriptions using electronic prescription charts
audits.standard: Legal prescribing requirements (Medicines Act 1968), trust Medicines Management Policy; ten standards based on RCP Generic Medical Record Keeping Standards 2017
audits.setting: Four inpatient paediatric wards using electronic prescribing

cycle1.result: 100% compliance for most demographics and prescription items and all fluid standards; allergy status 95% (severity 93%); weight 73%; antimicrobial indication 81% and duration 46%.

audits.intervention: Results presented locally and emailed to staff; recommended e-prescribing training and compulsory weight and allergy entry.
audits.other_findings: Electronic prescribing improved adherence compared with previous paper chart audits.
audits.citation: Philippa S, Abimbola S. P37 Audit on the quality of documentation of paediatric prescriptions using electronic prescription charts. Archives of Disease in Childhood. 2018;103(2):e1.41-e1. doi:10.1136/archdischild-2017-314584.46.

audits.title: Medication charts and consent to treatment documentation audit in an acute mixed in-patient psychiatry unit in south Manchester
audits.standard: Local GMMH medication chart policy standards, plus capacity assessment and consent to treatment forms
audits.setting: Acute mixed inpatient psychiatry unit, south Manchester, Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Capacity assessment form 22 (71%); consent to treatment form 16 (52%); route recorded in 40% of depot prescriptions; regular medications date of administration 84%, signature 29%; allergy reaction recorded in 6/21 (29%)

audits.other_findings: PRN administration details were 100% complete; patient identifiers were not maintained beyond page 1. Re-audit planned in 3-6 months.
audits.citation: Mitra M, Hussain S, Raynor E, Wong J, Thom J. Medication charts and consent to treatment documentation audit in an acute mixed in-patient psychiatry unit in south Manchester. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S335-S335.

audits.title: Time to Rectify the Neglect? Audit on Prescription Writing the Neglected skill. Audit Ref No: AU/006/01/2021
audits.standard: BMA, BNF and trust prescription writing standards (GMC number, signature, doctor name, drug, indication, dose, route, frequency, dates, timings)
audits.setting: Victoria Ward, old age psychiatry, Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Errors found in all parameters except medication timings

audits.intervention: Results presented at departmental meeting and re-training on prescription writing

cycle2.result: Errors increased: GMC number errors up 20.33%, doctor name 16.87%, indication 12.94%, original start date 5%; name of drug improved by 10.88%

audits.other_findings: After the audit the trust issued stamps with GMC number and doctor's name; re-audit planned 6 months after stamps and quarterly training for new trainees.
audits.citation: Fulmali A, Sheik S, Suleman A, Rana F, Bloxam R, Abdallah L, et al.. Time to Rectify the Neglect? Audit on Prescription Writing the Neglected skill. Audit Ref No: AU/006/01/2021. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(Suppl 1):S154-S154.
